title.narrative: Provision of Multisectoral Humanitarian response in Health, Nutrition, WASH, GP/CP/GBV, and S/NFIs to IDPs affected by Sudanese War in El Fasher and famine in Shamal and Wasat Jebel Marra.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe conflict and famine in Central Darfur have severely impacted the Wasat and Shamal Jabel Marra localities, causing significant displacement, loss of livelihoods, deteriorating living conditions and high rates of malnutrition. This project targets 178, 959 (65, 241women, 44, 338girls, 34, 481men, 34, 899 boys) individuals among which 80, 507 are IDPs, 73, 592 are host communities and 24, 860 are Returnee populations. The intervention is led by a consortium of five NGOs: World Relief (WR), Danish Refugee Council (DRC), Triangle Génération Humanitaire (TGH), Jebel Marra Charity Organization (JMCO), and HOPE. A multi-sectoral approach to emergency response is essential to meeting the needs of IDPs, returnees, and host community. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgtProject Objectives:lt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtHealth and Nutrition Services:lt/bgt Enhance access to primary healthcare (PHC) services for maternal and child health, disease management, immunization, and essential drugs by supporting six fixed health facilities and deploying three mobile clinics. Nutrition interventions will treat Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) among children under five and pregnant and lactating women, with community-based prevention led by trained volunteers. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgtWater, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH):lt/bgt Improve access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene services to reduce disease risks. Activities include rehabilitating water points, constructing latrines, and conducting hygiene awareness campaigns. The project will employ community-led total sanitation (CLTS) approaches to ensure sustainability and ownership.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgtProtection Mechanisms:lt/bgt Strengthen protection for women, girls, and children at risk of gender-based violence (GBV) and exploitation. Services include case management, psychosocial support, safe spaces, and referral pathways. General Protection (GP) will involve training community networks to monitor and address protection concerns, ensuring safety and dignity.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgtShelter and Non-Food Items (S/NFIs):lt/bgt Provide emergency shelter materials (plastic sheets, poles) and essential non-food items (blankets, sleeping mats, mosquito nets, and utensils) to 1,000 households. This will help families create safe living spaces and reduce GBV risks, with distribution processes emphasizing dignity, safeguarding, and accountability.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgtImplementation Strategy:lt/bgtltbrgtThe consortium will employ a coordinated, area-based approach, ensuring comprehensive sectoral coverage in targeted localities. Each partner will leverage its expertise and community relationships to ensure effective service delivery, conflict sensitivity, and equitable resource distribution. Community engagement, local authority consultations, and coordination with relevant clusters will align activities with humanitarian standards.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgtConflict Sensitivity and Social Cohesion:lt/bgtltbrgtAcknowledging the conflict dynamics in Central Darfur, the project will emphasize conflict-sensitive programming, working with community leaders and authorities to mitigate tensions and foster peaceful coexistence. A balanced resource allocation will ensure inclusivity and avoid perceptions of bias.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgtCross-Cutting Themes:lt/bgtltbrgtThe project will integrate cross-cutting themes like protection mainstreaming, gender equality, disability inclusion, and accountability to affected populations (AAP) across all activities to ensure a safe, inclusive, and responsive approach.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgtConsortium Partners and Collaboration:lt/bgtltbrgtThe consortium—WR, DRC, TGH, JMCO, and HOPE—will use their experience in Central Darfur to leverage local knowledge and networks. Regular coordination, joint monitoring, and evaluation will facilitate effective implementation, adaptability to needs, and achievement of outcomes.ltbrgtlt/pgt
